title: Onboard orion-lite-6b v1.1: metadata, perf profiles, and changelog automation
author: Liam Chen
description:
Motivation: onboard orion-lite-6b v1.1 into the model registry with complete metadata, verified performance profiles for our common latency/throughput buckets, and automated changelog/release-note generation so release engineering doesn't need to hand-edit entries. This PR includes model metadata updates (architecture/quantization/format), perf profiles generated from the perf-lab harness, revisions to the registry schema to accommodate the new quantized variants, and a small automation hook that appends a templated changelog entry to the generated CHANGELOG.md when a model entry is created or updated.

What this PR does: - Adds orion-lite-6b v1.1 metadata (id, family, topology, tokenizer, formats, recommended quantization profiles). - Adds performance profiles: latency P50/P95 for 1/4/8 sequence lengths across c5g/g4/dedicated pools and recommended batch sizes. - Adds a migration to normalize the "supported_formats" field to a list and documents compatibility notes. - Adds a changelog automation script (registry/tools/changelog_bot.py) that collects model metadata and perf highlights and appends a formatted release note. - Adds unit and integration tests for the new metadata fields and perf-profile parsing.

Checklist: - [x] Metadata schema updates and tests - [x] Perf profile generation and validation (perf-lab run id: pl-2026-02-12-1987) - [x] Changelog automation with linting enabled - [x] Review approvals from model-registry and perf teams - [x] CI green (minor flaky GPU perf test rerun)

Notes/assumptions: The perf profiles are sampled from dedicated perf lab runs and include both FP16 and 4-bit quantized variants. The automation is intentionally conservative: it appends a draft changelog entry and opens a draft release note PR for engineers to edit before publishing. This avoids surprise release notes for sensitive models.

Backwards compatibility: The migration normalizes an edge case where a single-format string was stored; consumers should handle list semantics. We included a compatibility shim for older registry clients in registry/compat/v1_format_shim.py.

Merge strategy: squash-merge after approvals and final CI pass.
